title: DCLab Bench: one shape for every evaluation result, each campaign in a layer, the free runner and the Admin page's Benchmark tab
request: The owner asked whether DCLab evaluates itself as a whole (the system, its AI, agents, LLMs and multi-agent team) and for one benchmark of our own, with tracking and improvement over time.
spec: Every result in evidence/campaigns read into one row shape with its verdict (pass, fail or not scored, never a silent failure), its counts with intervals, split, gate, cost and model; each campaign in one named layer; each layer judged red, amber, thin, green or empty from its suites' latest results with the reasons; a free runner that records each run once; the same view on the Admin page for the owner.
plan: survey every verdict shape the suites wrote
the BenchRow contract and the reader in dclab_core
fix the metrics ledger that read dict verdicts as failures
map every campaign to a layer and test that none is left out
a runner of the free suites that records each run once
the Admin page's Benchmark tab behind an owner-only route

decisions.decision: No weighted total score: each layer is red, amber, thin, green or empty with its reasons
decisions.why: a total would let green layers hide a red one; the owner needs to see what fails

decisions.decision: A result without a gate's verdict is not scored (amber), never a failure
decisions.why: most results are measurements without a gate; counting them as failures was the defect found in the metrics ledger

decisions.decision: The summary is computed when asked, not written as a generated file
decisions.why: a generated summary would go stale with every new result and make every package rerun it; the recorded runs are the only files

decisions.decision: The runner only runs scripted suites on dev, with live models off
decisions.why: sealed sets are read once and live runs cost money; a test checks the command list

change: dclab_core/bench.py (BenchRow v1, verdict_of, counts, rows_of, layer_status), dclab_core 0.153.0, CHANGELOG, schemas; dclab_rnd/bench/ (LAYER_OF, COMMANDS, evidence_rows, run, summary, the command line); dclab_rnd/agent_metrics.py (eval_rows uses verdict_of, older verdict rows read again once); dclab_rnd/agentic/pages/bench.py and the owner-only route in accounts/guard.py; views/admin.html Benchmark tab; Makefile bench and bench-read; docs/guides/BENCHMARK.md, docs/SYSTEM_EVALUATION.md, CLAUDE.md, the data catalog; tests/test_bench_core.py, tests/test_bench.py, tests/test_agent_metrics.py.

findings.defect: The metrics ledger counted every dict verdict as a failure
findings.scenario: an analyst result with verdict {gate, status: pass} was read as the text of the dict, which does not start with pass, so the scorecard showed a passing suite as failed
findings.cause: agent_metrics.eval_rows read str(doc.get('verdict')) and tested startswith('pass')
findings.fix: eval_rows reads the verdict with dclab_core.bench.verdict_of; a not-scored result is its own metric; verdict rows an older reader wrote are read again once and the later row wins

findings.defect: Counts stored under a part of the result were not read, so most layers showed no cases
findings.scenario: the agent suite keeps leaks_caught under summary.audit; the first reading found no count for it
findings.cause: counts looked only at the top of the result and the top of its summary
findings.fix: counts walks up to three levels and keeps at most a fixed number of counts per result

findings.defect: A later dev result hid a failed sealed result, and one decision point's result hid the others
findings.scenario: journeys_v1 had sealed v6 failing and later dev runs passing, and the suite read as a pass; decision_models_v1 counted only its last judged point
findings.cause: only the newest result of a whole campaign counted, though a campaign holds independent gates side by side
findings.fix: each split and decision point of a suite is its own track (track_of), judged by its own newest result

findings.defect: An undated result never counted as the newest
findings.scenario: search_v3's decision result carried no date and failed, but an older dated result without a verdict was read instead
findings.cause: an empty date sorted before every date
findings.fix: a track's results are ordered by their number first, then their date

findings.defect: A verdict made of pass and fail words per part read as not scored
findings.scenario: the time decisions wrote verdicts such as pooled fail and daily pass, and their failures showed as amber
findings.cause: the reader knew only the pass, passed and status keys of a dict verdict
findings.fix: when every text part of a dict verdict reads as pass or fail, any fail is a failure and all passes a pass

findings.defect: An old misread verdict stayed in a workspace's ledger forever
findings.scenario: a ledger holding the old reader's failure for a dict verdict the new reader cannot score kept showing the suite as failed
findings.cause: the new reader wrote nothing for such a verdict, so nothing replaced the old row
findings.fix: any verdict the reader cannot score is written as not scored, which replaces the older row

findings.defect: A misspelt layer recorded an empty run
findings.scenario: make bench with a layer name that has no suites wrote a run with no commands into the history
findings.cause: layers without free suites were silently dropped
findings.fix: an unknown or empty choice of layers is refused before anything runs

findings.defect: Two runs started in the same second could lose the second run's record after it had run
findings.scenario: two make bench runs on one commit in one second: the second fails only when it writes, after its suites ran
findings.cause: the record's name held only the second and the commit
findings.fix: the record's name also holds the process id

findings.defect: The route's owner-only rule was untested
findings.scenario: without its guard entry any member could read the route, since a read defaults to the read permission
findings.cause: no test checked the guard entry
findings.fix: a test checks the route needs the admin permission and that only the owner has it

findings.defect: A recorded baseline read as a gate passed
findings.scenario: the learning campaign's ok, baseline recorded result counted as a pass
findings.cause: an ok at the start of a verdict was read as a pass
findings.fix: an ok that records a baseline is not scored

findings.defect: The campaign agent's tests failed to load in their own environment
findings.scenario: the nightly full gate ran tests/test_agentic.py under .venv-agent and every test failed on a missing numpy
findings.cause: agent_metrics imported dclab_core at load time to read verdicts, and the package loads numpy, which the agent environment does not have
findings.fix: the import is made where verdicts are read, not when the module loads

measurements.name: the first reading of every recorded result
measurements.gate: a hand count of verdicts against the reader for several campaigns
measurements.result: the decision models campaign reads as its result files say (two passes, the rest failures); the exam's practice runs read as not scored; every campaign has a layer
limits: the reader trusts each suite's own verdict; it does not judge whether a gate was a good one
layers with mostly ungated measurements stay amber until those suites get gates

outcome: DCLab has one view of all its evaluations by layer and track, in the command line and on the Admin page, with the history of recorded runs; the honest first reading shows six layers red.
lessons: read the shapes the data really has before writing the reader: four verdict shapes and three places for counts were all in use
a dashboard that silently drops what it cannot read lies; unknown shapes must show as not scored
a campaign is not one measurement: splits and decision points inside it are separate gates, and the newest result of one must never stand for the others
risks: the layer of a campaign is a judgment in LAYER_OF and may need the owner's review
the software layer stays empty until the first make bench run is recorded
the runner's suites take long on this Mac and share its memory with everything else
